questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers

questions.explanation: Speed refers to how fast a computer processes instructions.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers

questions.explanation: Analogue computers measure continuous quantities.

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: A hospital intensive care machine measures a patient's temperature continuously and converts the readings into numbers for display. It is best classed as a

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: "Garbage in, garbage out" (GIGO) means that
options: wrong input data will give wrong output
a computer cannot store waste files
printers print rubbish when out of ink
deleted files are kept in the Recycle Bin
computers create errors on their own

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem: Which of these is the main limitation of computers when compared with human beings?
options: They cannot store large amounts of data for more than a few days at a time
They work too slowly for business use
They cannot carry out repeated tasks
They can only work with numbers below one million

questions.stem: Which port is most commonly used today to connect a keyboard, mouse or flash drive to a computer?

Updates fix security weaknesses and errors found in earlier versions

questions.stem: A shop has sales of N12,500, N8,000 and N9,500 in three days. Which formula and result give the average daily sales if the values are in B2:B4?
A single page in a presentation is called a

questions.explanation: F5 starts the show from the beginning.

questions.stem: A pre-designed set of colours, fonts and backgrounds applied to slides is a

questions.stem: Which view shows small pictures of all the slides at once so that their order can easily be rearranged?

questions.stem: The movement of a picture flying onto a slide while the slide is being shown is a

questions.stem: The boxes with dotted borders on a new slide, such as "Click to add title", are called

questions.stem: The worldwide network of interconnected computer networks is the

questions.stem: A website's starting page is called its

questions.stem: Which of these is a search engine?

questions.stem: Text or an image on a web page that takes the user to another page when clicked is a

questions.stem: A bank runs web pages and staff messaging on its own internal network that outsiders cannot reach. Such a network is an

questions.stem: Saving a song from a music website onto the memory of a phone is an example of

questions.stem: The domain ending ".ng" in a web address shows that the site is

questions.explanation: Quotation marks search for an exact phrase.

Files are stored only in the RAM of the user's computer and vanish when it is switched off

questions.topic: Introduction to Basic ICT Concepts and Computers
questions.stem:
(a) Define a computer. [2 marks]
(b) Explain five characteristics of a computer. [10 marks]
(c) Classify computers by type, naming and briefly describing the three classes. [6 marks]
(d) State two limitations of computers. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: an electronic device that accepts data, processes it under the control of stored instructions and produces information
2 marks: speed: processes millions of instructions per second
2 marks: accuracy: produces correct results if input and program are correct
2 marks: diligence: works continuously without tiredness
2 marks: storage: keeps large volumes of data for later use
2 marks: automation/versatility: carries out tasks automatically / does many types of work
2 marks: analogue: works on continuously varying quantities, e.g. thermometer-type measuring systems
2 marks: digital: works on discrete values (0 and 1), e.g. personal computers
2 marks: hybrid: combines analogue and digital features, e.g. hospital monitoring equipment
1 mark: cannot think or take decisions on its own
1 mark: depends on electricity / GIGO / cannot correct wrong input
questions.explanation: A computer is an electronic machine that accepts data, processes it according to stored instructions and gives out information. Characteristics include speed, accuracy, diligence, large storage, automation and versatility. By type, computers are analogue (continuous quantities), digital (discrete binary values) or hybrid (both). They cannot think for themselves, depend on power and produce wrong output from wrong input.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between primary and secondary storage. [4 marks]
(b) Name four examples of secondary storage devices. [4 marks]
(c) Give three differences between RAM and ROM. [6 marks]
(d) A student has a 64 GB flash drive containing 18.5 GB of files. She wants to copy 30 video files of 1.5 GB each onto it. Calculate (i) the total size of the videos; (ii) whether they will fit, showing the free space after copying or the shortfall. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: primary storage (main memory) is directly accessed by the CPU and holds data/programs in use
2 marks: secondary storage holds data permanently for later use and is not directly accessed by the CPU
1 mark: hard disk drive
1 mark: solid-state drive / flash drive
1 mark: CD / DVD
1 mark: memory card / magnetic tape
2 marks: RAM is volatile; ROM is non-volatile
2 marks: RAM can be read and written; ROM is mainly read only
2 marks: RAM holds current programs and data; ROM holds start-up (BIOS/firmware) instructions
2 marks: 30 x 1.5 = 45 GB
2 marks: free space = 64 - 18.5 = 45.5 GB
2 marks: they fit, leaving 0.5 GB free
questions.explanation: Primary memory (RAM, ROM, cache) is accessed directly by the CPU; secondary storage (HDD, SSD, flash drive, DVD, memory card) stores data permanently. RAM is volatile and read-write, holding running programs; ROM is non-volatile, mostly read-only, holding start-up firmware. Videos = 30 x 1.5 = 45 GB; free space = 64 - 18.5 = 45.5 GB, so they fit with 0.5 GB left.

questions.stem:
(a) Define system software and application software. [4 marks]
(b) Explain four functions of an operating system. [8 marks]
(c) Distinguish between proprietary software and open-source software, giving one example of each. [6 marks]
(d) State two ways of obtaining software legally. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: system software controls/manages the computer and provides a platform for other programs
2 marks: application software performs specific tasks for users
2 marks: process management: allocating processor time to tasks
2 marks: memory management: allocating and freeing memory
2 marks: file management: creating, organising and protecting files and folders
2 marks: device management / user interface / security
2 marks: proprietary software is owned and licensed; its source code is kept secret and use is restricted
2 marks: open-source software has source code freely available to view, modify and share
1 mark: proprietary example: Microsoft Windows / Microsoft Office
1 mark: open-source example: Linux / LibreOffice / Firefox
1 mark: buying a licence from the developer or authorised dealer
1 mark: downloading from official websites/app stores / using free or open-source software
questions.explanation: System software (OS, utilities, drivers, translators) runs the computer; application software (word processors, games, payroll) serves users. The OS manages processes, memory, files, devices, security and the user interface. Proprietary software such as Windows is licensed and its code is closed; open-source software such as Linux or LibreOffice has public code. Software is obtained legally by buying licences, using official stores or free/open-source sources.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a computer virus? [2 marks]
(b) State four symptoms of a virus-infected computer. [4 marks]
(c) Explain four ways of preventing virus infection. [8 marks]
(d) Identify three health hazards associated with prolonged computer use and suggest a remedy for each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: a malicious program that attaches itself to other files and replicates, often damaging data or the system
1 mark: the computer becomes unusually slow
1 mark: files disappear or become corrupted
1 mark: strange messages or pop-ups appear
1 mark: programs crash or refuse to open / the computer restarts unexpectedly
2 marks: install antivirus software and keep it updated
2 marks: scan flash drives and downloads before opening them
2 marks: avoid opening e-mail attachments or links from unknown senders
2 marks: use a firewall / download from trusted sources / keep the OS updated
1 mark: eye strain
1 mark: remedy: take regular breaks, adjust brightness, use anti-glare screens
1 mark: back and neck pain
1 mark: remedy: use adjustable chairs and correct posture
1 mark: repetitive strain injury
1 mark: remedy: wrist rests, ergonomic keyboards, breaks
questions.explanation: A virus is malicious code that attaches to files, copies itself and may damage data. Signs include slowness, missing or corrupted files, odd messages and crashes. Prevent infection with updated antivirus software, scanning removable media, caution with attachments and links, firewalls and system updates. Health hazards: eye strain (breaks, brightness), back/neck pain (ergonomic chairs, posture), RSI (wrist rests, breaks).

questions.stem:
(a) Define the Internet. [2 marks]
(b) Explain four services available on the Internet. [8 marks]
(c) State four requirements for connecting a home computer to the Internet. [4 marks]
(d) Give three advantages and three disadvantages of the Internet to secondary school students. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: a global network of interconnected computer networks that communicate using standard protocols (TCP/IP)
2 marks: World Wide Web: access to linked web pages
2 marks: e-mail: sending and receiving electronic messages
2 marks: e-learning / online research
2 marks: social media, e-commerce, file transfer or video conferencing
1 mark: a computer or smartphone
1 mark: a modem or router (or mobile data device)
1 mark: subscription with an Internet Service Provider
1 mark: a web browser / communication software
1 mark: advantage: research and access to information
1 mark: advantage: e-learning and online classes
1 mark: advantage: communication with teachers and peers
1 mark: disadvantage: exposure to harmful or inappropriate content
1 mark: disadvantage: addiction/time-wasting
1 mark: disadvantage: cyberbullying, fraud or plagiarism
questions.explanation: The Internet is a worldwide network of networks using TCP/IP. Services include the WWW, e-mail, e-learning, social media, e-commerce, file transfer and video conferencing. A connection needs a device, a modem/router or mobile data, an ISP subscription and a browser. Students gain information, online lessons and communication, but face harmful content, addiction, cyberbullying, scams and plagiarism.

questions.stem:
(Test of practical knowledge) Describe the steps for each of the following in a word processor:
(a) inserting a 4-column by 5-row table; [3 marks]
(b) changing the paper size of a document to A4 and the orientation to landscape; [3 marks]
(c) checking the spelling of the whole document; [2 marks]
(d) inserting a picture from a file. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: place the cursor where the table is required
1 mark: click Insert > Table
1 mark: select/enter 4 columns and 5 rows and click OK
1 mark: click Layout (Page Layout) tab
1 mark: Size > A4
1 mark: Orientation > Landscape
1 mark: click Review > Spelling and Grammar (or press F7)
1 mark: accept/ignore/change each suggestion until complete
1 mark: Insert > Pictures > This Device
1 mark: locate the picture and click Insert
questions.explanation: Table: cursor in place, Insert > Table > Insert Table, 4 columns, 5 rows, OK. Paper: Layout > Size > A4; Layout > Orientation > Landscape. Spelling: Review > Spelling & Grammar or F7, act on each suggestion. Picture: Insert > Pictures > This Device, choose file, Insert.

questions.stem:
(Test of practical knowledge) A worksheet holds the following marks: A2: Uche, B2: 62, C2: 75; A3: Halima, B3: 48, C3: 59; A4: Tunde, B4: 81, C4: 70; A5: Esther, B5: 55, C5: 44. Column B is Test 1 and column C is Test 2.
(a) Write the formula for the total of Uche in D2 and state its value. [2 marks]
(b) Write the formula for the average of Uche in E2 and state its value. [2 marks]
(c) Calculate the totals that will appear in D3, D4 and D5 after the formula in D2 is copied down. [3 marks]
(d) Write a formula in F2 that shows "PASS" if E2 is 50 or more and "FAIL" otherwise, and state the students who will FAIL. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: =B2+C2 or =SUM(B2:C2)
1 mark: 137
1 mark: =AVERAGE(B2:C2) or =D2/2
1 mark: 68.5
1 mark: D3 = 107
1 mark: D4 = 151
1 mark: D5 = 99
2 marks: =IF(E2>=50,"PASS","FAIL")
1 mark: Esther fails (average 49.5); all others pass
questions.explanation: Uche: 62 + 75 = 137, average 68.5. Halima 107 (53.5), Tunde 151 (75.5), Esther 99 (49.5). =IF(E2>=50,"PASS","FAIL") gives FAIL only for Esther.

questions.stem:

(b) apply the same transition to all slides; [3 marks]

questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Home > New Slide
1 mark: Home > Layout
1 mark: choose Two Content
1 mark: click Transitions tab
1 mark: select a transition effect
1 mark: click Apply To All

questions.stem:
(Test of practical knowledge)
(a) Describe how to create a new free e-mail account. [4 marks]
(b) Describe how to download an attachment from a received e-mail and save it in a folder. [3 marks]
(c) State three things a user should do before clicking a link in an e-mail. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: open a browser and go to the e-mail provider's website
1 mark: click Create account / Sign up
1 mark: fill in name, preferred user name, password and recovery details
1 mark: agree to terms, verify (e.g. by phone code) and finish
1 mark: open the e-mail with the attachment
1 mark: click the download icon on the attachment
1 mark: choose the folder in the Save dialog and click Save
1 mark: check that the sender's address is genuine
1 mark: hover over the link to see the real web address
1 mark: be wary of urgent requests for passwords or money / scan with antivirus
questions.explanation: Go to the provider's site, click Create account, enter details and a strong password, verify and finish. Open the message, click the attachment's download icon and save to the chosen folder. Before clicking links, confirm the sender, hover to inspect the address, and be cautious of urgent requests for passwords, PINs or money.

questions.stem:
(Test of practical knowledge) A school has just bought a desktop computer, a printer and a UPS.
(a) Describe how the devices should be connected and powered on for the first time. [4 marks]
(b) Describe how to install the printer using its driver. [3 marks]
(c) State three precautions to take when handling the computer and its accessories. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: connect monitor, keyboard and mouse to the system unit
1 mark: connect the printer by USB (or network) cable
1 mark: connect the system unit and monitor to the UPS and the UPS to the wall socket
1 mark: switch on socket, UPS, then monitor, system unit and printer
1 mark: insert driver disc or download the driver from the manufacturer's website
1 mark: run the set-up program and follow the prompts
1 mark: print a test page to confirm installation
1 mark: switch off power before connecting or disconnecting cables
1 mark: avoid food, drinks and dust near the equipment
1 mark: handle parts gently / do not block ventilation / use surge protection
questions.explanation: Connect peripherals to the system unit, plug the computer into the UPS and the UPS into the socket, then switch on in order. Install the printer with its driver (disc or website), run set-up and print a test page. Precautions: power off before connecting cables, keep away food and dust, handle gently and keep vents clear.
